::: {#thm-substitution-logic}
#### Replacing a part by an equivalent part

If $A$ and $B$ are [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent), $A \equiv B$,
then replacing $A$ by $B$ inside a larger proposition
gives a proposition logically equivalent to the larger one.
In particular, $\neg A \equiv \neg B$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

The truth value of the larger proposition in a row of its truth table
depends on the truth value of $A$ in that row, not on how $A$ is written.
$A$ and $B$ have the same truth value in every row,
so the two larger propositions do too.

:::

:::
